title: Q2 evidence gap + June-only public-store subcohort
scope: Full Q2 (April 1–June 30) supply, >=1,000-review hit counts and rates are unavailable. The separate June-only panel is a September public-store snapshot of apps with displayed June release dates, not a Chris/HTMAG cohort extension.
methodology: Searched and read the public HTMAG 2026 archive and relevant Q2/Summer posts. No complete public Q2 genre supply/hit table or underlying public cohort sheet was located by September 2.

WN Hub's first-half report uses a different time period and revenue metric; its detailed genre analysis is subscription-gated. It cannot safely supply Q2 review-based rates or be differenced against HTMAG Q1.

A bounded anonymous US/English public Steam catalogue retrieval saved 30 contiguous 100-result pages, then stopped after an HTTP error. The saved dates bracket June, but do not cover April and most of May.

Filter saved responses to app item keys with displayed dates June 1–30, exclude packages, deduplicate app IDs, and retain every app regardless of review count, price, studio size, or tags. No-title/no-review exclusions are applied.

Assign each app to any selected tag present in its search-response tag IDs (up to seven). This is overlapping tag classification, not the manual single-genre method used by Chris. The Indie tag is not used as a studio-size filter.

A numerical displayed review-score count >=1,000 establishes a confirmed minimum across languages, even if the displayed count is English-only. A non-language-specific numerical count below 1,000 is below this scored-review threshold. Language-specific sub-1,000 counts and absent numerical tooltips remain unresolved, not zero.

No per-game all-language review API batch was run after the catalogue fetch stopped. Therefore exact hit rates remain null. Lower/upper bounds are only arithmetic bounds within the included June-tagged rows, not statistical confidence intervals or full-Q2 probabilities.

caveats: Not a full-Q2 table. June cannot be scaled to April–June and should not be shown as a quarter-over-quarter trend against HTMAG 2025 or Q1 2026.

June is bracketed within the saved search sequence, but anonymous US visibility, removed/restricted products, content preferences and live pagination can omit games. Complete Steam coverage is not claimed.
Displayed release dates may reflect full release after earlier Early Access. Lifetime reviews can predate June. This is not a cohort of first-ever commercial releases or reviews earned during June.
Reviews were observed September 2, 64–93 days after June dates. HTMAG Q1 used an April 2 snapshot; the observation windows and maturity differ.

Review-score counts are not all review posts, units, revenue, wishlists, or organic reach. Steam excludes nonqualifying purchase types and some off-topic activity from the score. Marketing spend is not observed.

No numerical tooltip is not proven to mean zero reviews. These rows stay in the denominator and their review-threshold status remains unresolved; consequently the bounds can be too wide to rank genres usefully.

Tag assignment uses only the up-to-seven returned IDs, not all visible tags or a single best-fit genre. Rows overlap and must not be added together. Idler is not the entire incremental category; Bullet Hell is not synonymous with bullet heaven; Online Co-Op is not friendslop.
Paid and free games, indies and large studios are mixed. A low count is not proof of commercial failure, and a high count is not evidence of profit, affordable scope, or causal organic marketing.

Exact full-quarter data needs a legitimately available complete export plus consistent release/EA, purchase-type, language, tag and snapshot rules. No paywall, authentication, CAPTCHA or rate-limit workaround was used.
